narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Luke; measured, orderly storytelling, including the words that introduce speech.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Jesus of Nazareth on the way to Jerusalem and in the temple; calm authority, teaching in parables, warning and healing.

rich-man.name: The rich ruler
rich-man.note: A wealthy ruler asking about everlasting life; respectful and sincere, sure of his own observance.

bystanders.name: Bystanders
bystanders.note: Those who heard the saying about the rich; dismayed, asking who can be saved.

peter.name: Peter
peter.note: Apostle; speaking up for the twelve, a little anxious about what they have given up.

bartimaeus.name: The blind man of Jericho
bartimaeus.note: The blind beggar by the wayside near Jericho (Bartimaeus in Mark; unnamed in Luke); shouting insistently over the crowd, then simple and trusting.

1.t: And he spoke also a parable to them, that we ought always to pray and not to faint,

2.t: There was a judge in a certain city, who feared not God nor regarded man.

3.t: And there was a certain widow in that city; and she came to him, saying: Avenge me of my adversary.

4.t: And he would not for a long time. But afterwards he said within himself: Although I fear not God nor regard man,

5.t: Yet because this widow is troublesome to me, I will avenge her, lest continually coming she weary me.

6.t: Hear what the unjust judge saith.

7.t: And will not God revenge his elect who cry to him day and night? And will he have patience in their regard?

8.t: I say to you that he will quickly revenge them. But yet the Son of man, when he cometh, shall he find, think you, faith on earth?

9.t: And to some who trusted in themselves as just and despised others, he spoke also this parable:

10.t: Two men went up into the temple to pray: the one a Pharisee and the other a publican.

11.t: The Pharisee standing, prayed thus with himself: O God, I give thee thanks that I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, as also is this publican.

12.t: I fast twice in a week: I give tithes of all that I possess.

13.t: And the publican, standing afar off, would not so much as lift up his eyes towards heaven; but struck his breast, saying: O God, be merciful to me a sinner.

14.t: I say to you, this man went down into his house justified rather than the other: because every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

15.t: And they brought unto him also infants, that he might touch them. Which when the disciples saw, they rebuked them.

16.t: But Jesus, calling them together, said:
Suffer children to come to me and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

17.t: Amen, I say to you: Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a child shall not enter into it.

18.t: And a certain ruler asked him, saying:
Good master, what shall I do to possess everlasting life?

19.t: Why dost thou call me good? None is good but God alone.

20.t: Thou knowest the commandments: Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery: Thou shalt not steal: Thou shalt not bear false witness: Honour thy father and mother.

21.t: All these things have I kept from my youth.

22.t: Which when Jesus had heard, he said to him:
Yet one thing is wanting to thee. Sell all whatever thou hast and give to the poor: and thou shalt have treasure in heaven. And come, follow me.

23.t: He having heard these things, became sorrowful: for he was very rich.

24.t: And Jesus seeing him become sorrowful, said:
How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God

25.t: For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

26.t: And they that heard it said:

27.t: The things that are impossible with men are possible with God.

28.t: Behold, we have left all things and have followed thee.

29.t: Amen, I say to you, there is no man that hath left home or parents or brethren or wife or children, for the kingdom of God's sake,

30.t: Who shall not receive much more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.

31.t: Then Jesus took unto him the twelve and said to them:
Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and all things shall be accomplished which were written by the prophets concerning the Son of man.

32.t: For he shall be delivered to the Gentiles and shall be mocked and scourged and spit upon.

33.t: And after they have scourged him, they will put him to death. And the third day he shall rise again.

34.t: And they understood none of these things, and this word was hid from them: and they understood not the things that were said.

35.t: Now it came to pass, when he drew nigh to Jericho, that a certain blind man sat by the way side, begging.

36.t: And when he heard the multitude passing by, he asked what this meant.

37.t: And they told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.

38.t: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.

39.t: And they that went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out much more:
Son of David, have mercy on me.

40.t: And Jesus standing, commanded him to be brought unto him. And when he was come near, he asked him,

41.t: What wilt thou that I do to thee?

42.t: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath made thee whole.

43.t: And immediately he saw and followed him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
